data.name: Latifi
data.gender_notes: Latifi is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root letters 'L-T-F', meaning 'to give' or 'to bestow'. In Islamic tradition, Latifi represents the giver of blessings, the one who distributes goodness and mercy. The name Latifi carries the meaning “The Giver, Benefactor” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Latifi usually hope their child will grow to embody the giver, benefactor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the giving nature of Allah (SWT) and encourages the giver to be generous and compassionate towards others.
data.etymology: Latifi belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Giver, Benefactor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Latifi total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: لطيفي
in_arabic.meaning: اللطيف من أسماء الله الحسنى، يعني الرقيق الخفي
in_arabic.long_meaning: لطيفي اسم مشتق من اللطيف، وهو من أسماء الله الحسنى في الإسلام. يعني الاسم الرقيق الخفي الذي يعبر عن لطف الله تعالى وخفاياه التي لا يدركها إلا هو. يستخدم الاسم في بعض الأحيان لوصف الله تعالى بأنه اللطيف الخبير الذي يرى كل شيء ويفهم كل شيء.

in_urdu.long_meaning: لطیفی نام لطیف سے ماخوذ ہے، جو اللہ کے 99 ناموں میں سے ایک ہے۔ اس نام کا مطلب ہے نفیس پوشیدہ، جو اللہ کی لطافت اور پوشیدہ کاموں کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ یہ نام بعض اوقات اللہ کی لطافت اور خفایاکو بیان کرنے کے لیے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے۔

in_pashto.long_meaning: لطیفي نوم لطیف څخه اخیستل شوی دی، کوم چې د الله تعالی یو نوم دی. د دې نوم مطلب دقيق پټ دی، کوم چې د الله تعالی د لطف او پټو کارونو څرګندونه کوي. دا نوم کله کله د الله تعالی د لطف او پټو کارونو د څرګندولو لپاره کارول کیږي.

in_english.name: Latifi
in_english.meaning: Latifi means one of Allah's beautiful names, signifying subtle and hidden
in_english.long_meaning: The name Latifi is derived from Latif, one of the 99 names of Allah in Islam. It signifies 'subtle' or 'hidden', reflecting Allah's subtlety and hidden actions. This name is sometimes used to express Allah's gentle and mysterious nature. Historically, it has been used to describe the nuanced and concealed aspects of divine wisdom. In Islamic tradition, Latifi embodies the attributes of kindness, compassion, and benevolence.

Among Arab and Muslim communities, generosity is deemed an important virtue, and the name Latifi is a constant reminder of the importance of giving and sharing in daily life.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Latifi reflects the concept of Allah (God) as the ultimate giver of blessings, and the individual carrying this name is considered to be a vessel or a reflection of that divine attribute. The name serves as a reminder that we are all meant to give and share, not just with our immediate families and communities, but with all of humanity and indeed all of creation. In essence, Latifi evokes a sense of spiritual responsibility, encouraging the bearer to embody the qualities of compassion, kindness and selflessness at all times.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hadid mentions a scholar named Ali ibn al-Latif in his 'Muntazam fi tarikh al-Hidjaj', written between 1215 and 1242 AD. He was a prominent Andalusian scholar and jurist from the city of Cordoba, known for his knowledge in various fields including medicine, philosophy, and jurisprudence.

Al-Qalqashandi in his 'Subh al-Asha' mentions a famous calligrapher named Latif ibn Ibrahim, active in the late 14th and early 15th centuries in Egypt. He was a student of the renowned calligrapher Ibn al-Raslan and is considered one of the most accomplished calligraphers of the Mamluk period.
